content: Chiggers are microscopic, six-legged, wingless larvae that eventually develop into a type of mite. These organisms are commonly found in areas with tall grass, weeds, and other vegetation. Their bites result in intense itching. The primary symptoms of chigger bites include severe itching and the appearance of red, pimple-like bumps or hives. The itching sensation typically begins several hours after the chiggers attach to the skin. A rash may develop on areas of the body exposed to sunlight, often stopping at the point where underwear or tight clothing meets the skin. This pattern can serve as a diagnostic clue for chigger bites. Chiggers are most commonly encountered in outdoor environments such as berry patches, tall grass, weeds, and the edges of wooded areas. They tend to bite humans in areas like the waist, ankles, or warm skin folds. These bites are more frequent during the summer and fall months. A healthcare provider can diagnose chigger bites by visually examining the characteristic rash. It is advisable to seek medical attention if the itching becomes severe, if symptoms worsen, or if there is no improvement despite treatment. Treatment for chigger bites focuses on alleviating the itching. Over-the-counter antihistamines and corticosteroid creams or lotions are often effective in providing relief. Chigger bites typically resolve on their own without the need for medical intervention. However, intense scratching of the affected areas can lead to secondary bacterial infections, which represent a potential complication. To prevent chigger bites, it is recommended to avoid outdoor areas known to be infested with chiggers.
